newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds trim gains at close.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds trim gains at close.

text.p: Argentine bonds gave back some gains to close marginally higher Monday after mild profit-taking, dealers said.

"The market started off well on news that (Economy Minister Roque) Fernandez was considering the possibility of a debt buyback. But then it stalled and pulled back a little, and we could see some more light selling tomorrow," one dealer at a leading foreign bank said.
In an interview Monday Fernandez said "conditions are right" for Argentina to buy back foreign debt for the first time, but gave no more details.
Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 closed up 3/8 at 94.875 while the dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 was flat at 121.
Traders a drop in U.S. long bond yields to 6.58 percent from 6.62 percent Thursday had underpinned the market.
"Local players may be tempted to take profits tomorrow at these levels, but we don't expect any sharp fall because liquidity remains strong," another dealer said.
